text:
Luke Hughes scored six goals in 68 games last season. He has six in 18 this season, and the Devils have won nine of his last ten games, the last five in a row. He's playing 24.4 minutes a night, and New Jersey takes 56% of the 5v5 expected goals with him on.

The goals won't keep coming at this rate. He's shooting 14% after 4% last season, on just 3.2 expected goals, against a talent range centred around 6.5%. Our projection settles him at about 16 goals and 47 points, which would still be a big step forward.

The Hockey News' Mike Fink wrote this week that Hughes is becoming an elite defenseman. The case against is in his own end: Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.17 more expected goals per 60 with him on last season, bottom 3% of defensemen. Then there was Saturday's fight with the Islanders' Matthew Schaefer, covered by TSN, the New York Post and others, with RMNB's headline adding "Hockey is an emotional sport." The night ended with a Jack Hughes overtime winner.
headline: Luke Hughes is scoring like a forward, for now
